risk_if_not_implemented: Without Physical Tampering Detection, counterfeit, non-conforming or compromised components and services may enter the environment through the supply chain. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity (R-AM-2), Undetected / Delayed Detection of Adverse Activity (R-SA-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Physical Crime (MT-5), Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14).

compensating_control_1.name: Monitoring Physical Access
compensating_control_1.description: Physical access control mechanisms exist to monitor for, detect and respond to physical security incidents.
compensating_control_1.justification: Monitoring Physical Access (PES-13) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Physical Tampering Detection (AST-29.1) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
